name: GPU kernel workbench
scenario: A systems student has a reusable timing harness and good estimates for routine kernels. Debugging apparently tiny synchronization or indexing bugs has highly variable durations.

tasks.title: Add the fused bias baseline
tasks.description: Extend an existing elementwise addition kernel with one bias read and reuse the correctness harness at three sizes.
tasks.details: Benchmark script already accepts a third argument.

tasks.title: Fix the reduction tail failure
tasks.description: Track down sporadic mismatches when the last reduction tile is partial. Add tests for prime lengths after identifying the bug.
tasks.details: Only one test is flaky; I have not isolated the input yet.

sections.heading: Symptom
sections.body: An array of length 1009 usually matches the host sum; repeated launches occasionally differ. Multiples of the block size pass. The current test runner checks only one launch per input.

sections.heading: Reproducer
sections.body: Sweep lengths on either side of a tile boundary with a fixed random seed. Compare the first differing block against a CPU partial-sum trace.

sections.heading: Done
sections.body: Provide a reproducible failure, a patch, and a regression that passes over 200 launches. Do not change the comparison tolerance.

tasks.title: Refresh the transfer table
tasks.description: Run the existing host/device bandwidth benchmark on three batch sizes and update the table.
tasks.details: The node is booked and the harness is installed.

tasks.title: Implement the straightforward strided gather
tasks.description: Use the provided index equation for each lane; validate against the NumPy reference and add the kernel to the benchmark.
tasks.details: No shared memory or tuning pass requested.

tasks.title: Diagnose transposed labels
tasks.description: Figure out why non-square batches swap two output channels in the profiler build. Patch the bad dimension and test both layouts.
tasks.details: This appears isolated to the host dispatch.

tasks.title: Isolate the scratch-buffer race
tasks.description: Create the smallest repeatable failure with two streams and fix the lifetime of a shared temporary allocation.
tasks.details: No stable reproduction yet. Include the 100-run test.

tasks.title: Compare block sizes for the gather
tasks.description: Use the fixed workload and harness to time four block sizes. Report medians and keep the fastest passing setting.
tasks.details: No new kernel algorithm. Test the same four choices on every shape.

tasks.title: Add optional mask to bias kernel
tasks.description: Reuse the elementwise baseline and add output checks for one sparse and one dense mask.
tasks.details: The reference and parameter plumbing are done.

holdouts.title: Triage a sporadic normalization mismatch
holdouts.description: Find and fix a discrepancy visible only when two request streams overlap. Leave behind a regression that fails reliably before the patch.
holdouts.details: Unknown cause. The single-stream benchmark is clean.

sections.heading: Evidence
sections.body: The same input yields correct normalized outputs with one stream and occasional differences with two. Launch order and buffer pool events are available as timestamped records.

sections.heading: Scope
sections.body: Keep both streams active. Create a reproducer with the smallest batch you can find and locate the first incorrect intermediate. Document any assumption about buffer ownership.

sections.heading: Acceptance
sections.body: Submit the fix, the failing replay, and a repeated correctness run. Speed measurements are optional.

holdouts.check: Similar unknown-cause debugging tasks have a broad spread; a precise estimate matching routine implementation would be misleading.

holdouts.title: Sweep normalization block sizes
holdouts.description: Measure four block sizes with the existing script on the six known-good shapes and update the throughput table.
holdouts.details: Correctness is already established. Use the reserved node and record medians.
holdouts.check: Retrieve scripted sweeps, then check whether a correction helps a task whose original budget happened to be accurate.
